completion_data.completion_summary: Narrowed lean-plan-compliance-check.sh's Goals-prose fallback harvest to a per-bullet leading-identifier-run (matching plan-format.md's documented contract and lean-challenge-snapshot.sh's sibling implementation), using possessive quantifiers to fix a PCRE backtracking artifact discovered during verification. Re-baselined C13-C16, added regression cases C20-C22, and corrected a stale fixture comment. Test suite grew from 19 to 22 cases, all green; the sibling snapshot suite's 37 cases are unchanged.

memory_candidates.content: When porting a plain `grep -oP '^\s*MARKER\s*\K(?:ALTERNATION)+'` single-regex extraction where one branch of ALTERNATION accepts the same character class as the preceding \s*, PCRE backtracking can donate characters from the \s* prefix into the alternation to satisfy a `+` quantifier that would otherwise fail to match zero-width content -- producing a spurious non-empty match on input the pattern was meant to reject entirely. Fix: make the prefix quantifiers POSSESSIVE (`\s*+`) rather than greedy, which forbids backtracking into them. Always verify any single-regex port of a two-step Python re.match/re.match sequence against the exact 'no match at all' input case, not just the 'matches something' cases.

Before writing a test assertion against a script's 'which code path was taken' narrative (e.g. 'assert the harvest source'), grep the production script for every echo/print of the variable in question -- it may only be emitted on one of several verdict branches (e.g. only on 'skipped', never on 'passed'/'failed'). When the direct string isn't observable on the branch under test, discharge the assertion structurally instead (exact-set/count assertions that could only hold if the intended code path ran) and document the substitution in the test's own header comment.

sapience_notes.subject: lean-plan-compliance-check.sh Goals-prose fallback harvest
sapience_notes.value: Narrowed the script to match plan-format.md's documented per-bullet leading-identifier-run contract (rejected alternative: widen the document to codify the script's old over-broad behavior). This was the third narrowing of this one harvest, after a reserved-keyword denylist and a colon-optional Goals-range widening -- recorded as evidence that narrowing the harvest, not constraining Goals prose, is this codebase's established remedy pattern for this class of defect.

sapience_notes.subject: grep -P (PCRE) quantifier backtracking across \K
sapience_notes.value: A pattern of the shape `^\s*MARKER\s*\K(?:X|[\s,/]|...)+` where the alternation includes a whitespace-matching branch will backtrack the preceding \s* to donate a character into the `+` alternation whenever the content immediately after MARKER does not itself match any alternative -- producing a one-character spurious match (the donated whitespace) instead of a correct zero-match/no-match result. Possessive quantifiers (`\s*+`) on the prefix eliminate this backtracking. Confirmed live with `grep -oP` against a real prose-leading-bullet input; the equivalent sequential two-regex form (Python's separate re.match calls for bullet-marker then leading-run) does not exhibit this bug because the two matches are independent operations with no shared backtracking state.

sapience_notes.subject: Claude Code harness Bash tool auto-backgrounding threshold
sapience_notes.value: An ordinary foreground Bash call that produces no stdout for roughly 180 seconds gets auto-backgrounded by the harness regardless of the Bash tool's own `timeout` parameter (observed with the parameter explicitly set to 600000ms) and regardless of an inner shell `timeout` set below that value. The effective ceiling for a silent foreground wait appears to be a fixed ~180s idle/runtime threshold, not the declared tool timeout. Workaround: cap the inner shell timeout at ~170s per call and repeat the bounded kill -0 liveness-check call across successive tool invocations until the watched PID exits.

sapience_notes.subject: Two independent Lean plan Goals-block readers (lean-plan-compliance-check.sh, lean-challenge-snapshot.sh)
sapience_notes.value: The two readers are deliberately independently implemented (bash/grep vs Python) under a 'SHARED FRAGILITY' cross-reference convention rather than unified into shared code. As of this task they agree on harvest BREADTH (both apply the per-bullet leading-identifier-run rule) but still disagree on accepted Goals-HEADER shape: lean-plan-compliance-check.sh's range anchor does not accept the list-item `- **Goals**:` form that lean-challenge-snapshot.sh's START_RE already accepts. This header-shape gap is a standing, deliberately deferred residual, not a regression from this task.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh scoped batch-gate check, run under a concurrent multi-task /orchestrate batch
sapience_notes.value: A verify-touched.sh invocation's own overall verdict line can report failure even when the captured/visible test output shows 0 failures, if the run spans several minutes on a shared working tree that concurrent sibling tasks are actively committing to -- the failing section can be above a truncated output window, or the failure can be transient tree-state flux rather than a real regression. An untruncated, full-log re-run immediately after returned a clean result. Lesson: capture verify-touched.sh output to a file in full (never pipe through `tail` when later diagnosis might be needed), and treat a solo failing signal from a long-running check on a shared, concurrently-mutated tree as provisional until corroborated by a clean re-run.
